items.q: The reforestation fund is facing a ______ of nearly two million dollars between what donors pledged and what they actually paid.
items.vi: Quỹ trồng lại rừng đang đối mặt với mức thiếu hụt gần hai triệu đô la giữa số tiền các nhà tài trợ cam kết và số tiền họ thực sự chi trả.
items.explanation: The clue of nearly two million dollars between what donors pledged and what they actually paid is a measured gap between an expected sum and a real one, which is a shortfall. ✗ scarcity — a general shortage of a resource (a scarcity of water), not a gap you can count; ✗ deficiency — a lack of something the body or system needs (a vitamin deficiency); ✗ dearth — an almost complete absence (a dearth of talent), never measured in dollars.

items.q: Once electric cars became fashionable, several oil companies were quick to ______, launching charging networks of their own.
items.vi: Khi xe điện trở nên thịnh hành, nhiều công ty dầu mỏ đã nhanh chóng chạy theo trào lưu, tự tung ra các mạng lưới trạm sạc của riêng mình.
items.explanation: The clue once electric cars became fashionable … quick to describes joining a trend after it has become popular = jump on the bandwagon. ✗ jump the gun — act too early, before the proper time – the opposite of following others; ✗ jump through hoops — go through many tiresome steps to get something; ✗ jump ship — suddenly leave an organisation or cause, but here the companies are joining, not leaving.

items.q: The burglars ______ in through the front door – it was still bolted from the inside when the police arrived.
items.vi: Bọn trộm không thể nào đã vào bằng cửa trước – cửa vẫn còn cài then từ bên trong khi cảnh sát đến.
items.explanation: The clue it was still bolted from the inside is proof that entry by the front door was impossible, so we need a confident past deduction: can't have + past participle. ✗ mightn't have come — only 'perhaps they didn't', far too weak with solid proof; ✗ needn't have come — 'they did come, but it was unnecessary', which makes no sense; ✗ shouldn't have come — criticises a past action as wrong, not a statement about what was possible.

items.q: Prosecutors decided to ______ charges against the chemical company after the spill was traced to its pipeline.
items.vi: Các công tố viên quyết định khởi tố công ty hóa chất sau khi vụ rò rỉ được xác định bắt nguồn từ đường ống của công ty này.
items.explanation: Charges are brought (or pressed) against someone – a fixed legal collocation, signalled by prosecutors … charges against. ✗ raise — collocates with objections, questions or concerns, not charges; ✗ put — you put a question or a case to someone; 'put charges' is not English; ✗ make — you make an accusation or a complaint, but charges are not 'made'.

items.q: The city's recycling scheme has failed to ______ the expectations of the residents who campaigned so hard for it.
items.vi: Chương trình tái chế của thành phố đã không đáp ứng được kỳ vọng của những cư dân đã vận động hết mình cho nó.
items.explanation: The clue failed to ______ the expectations needs the phrasal verb meaning 'be as good as what was hoped': live up to. ✗ live down — make people forget a past embarrassment (he never lived down that mistake); ✗ live off — depend on something or someone for money or food (live off his parents); ✗ live through — survive a difficult period (live through the war).

items.q: The council inspects its flood defences only once in a ______ moon, ______ neighbouring towns check theirs every spring.
items.vi: Hội đồng thành phố hiếm hoi lắm mới kiểm tra hệ thống đê chắn lũ, trong khi các thị trấn lân cận kiểm tra hàng năm vào mỗi mùa xuân.
items.explanation: The idiom is once in a blue moon = very rarely, and the two clauses contrast (only once … / every spring), so the second blank needs the contrast conjunction whereas. ✗ full / whereas — 'once in a full moon' is not an idiom; ✗ blue / despite — despite must be followed by a noun or -ing, not a clause with a subject and verb; ✗ new / while — while could join the clauses, but 'once in a new moon' is not the idiom.

items.q: The courts are still struggling to clear a ______ of more than sixty thousand cases that built up during the pandemic.
items.vi: Các tòa án vẫn đang chật vật giải quyết lượng tồn đọng hơn sáu mươi nghìn vụ án tích tụ trong đại dịch.
items.explanation: The clues clear and cases that built up during the pandemic point to overdue work that has piled up: a backlog. ✗ stockpile — a large supply deliberately stored for future use (a stockpile of weapons); ✗ reserve — a supply kept back until it is needed (oil reserves); ✗ surplus — an amount left over beyond what is needed (a budget surplus) – none of these means unfinished work.

items.q: ______ the vaccine had been tested on ten thousand volunteers did the regulator agree to license it.
items.vi: Chỉ sau khi vắc-xin được thử nghiệm trên mười nghìn tình nguyện viên, cơ quan quản lý mới đồng ý cấp phép cho nó.
items.explanation: The inverted main clause did the regulator agree comes after a full subordinate clause (the vaccine had been tested …), which is the pattern Only after + clause + inverted main clause. ✗ Not only — inversion must follow it immediately (Not only had the vaccine …) and it needs 'but also' later; ✗ Hardly — needs immediate inversion and a 'when' clause (Hardly had … when); ✗ Seldom — needs immediate inversion (Seldom did …) and gives no time sequence.

items.q: The minister meant to unveil the carbon tax in June, but a careless tweet from an aide ______ three weeks early.
options: let the cat out of the bag
let the grass grow under his feet
items.answer: let the cat out of the bag
items.vi: Bộ trưởng định công bố thuế các-bon vào tháng Sáu, nhưng một dòng tweet bất cẩn của trợ lý đã để lộ bí mật sớm ba tuần.
items.explanation: The clue meant to unveil … in June, but a careless tweet … three weeks early describes a secret revealed by accident = let the cat out of the bag. ✗ let sleeping dogs lie — avoid stirring up an old problem; ✗ let off steam — release anger or energy in a harmless way; ✗ let the grass grow under his feet — waste time by delaying – the opposite of acting early.

items.q: The union insisted that every worker ______ issued with protective clothing before entering the contaminated site.
items.vi: Công đoàn khăng khăng yêu cầu mọi công nhân phải được cấp quần áo bảo hộ trước khi vào khu vực bị ô nhiễm.
items.explanation: Insisted that (like demand, suggest, recommend + that) is followed by the bare subjunctive, so the verb stays in its base form whatever the tense of the main clause: (should) be issued. ✗ were — the past subjunctive belongs after wish / if / as though, not after insist that; ✗ has been — an ordinary present perfect breaks the subjunctive pattern and clashes with past 'insisted'; ✗ will be — a future tense is not used in the that-clause after a verb of demand.

items.q: The evidence against the ringleader was ______ – fingerprints, CCTV footage and two eyewitnesses who picked him out of a line-up.
items.vi: Bằng chứng chống lại kẻ cầm đầu là quá rõ ràng và áp đảo – dấu vân tay, hình ảnh camera an ninh và hai nhân chứng đã nhận diện được hắn.
items.explanation: Overwhelming evidence is the collocation for proof too strong to resist, and the list fingerprints, CCTV footage and two eyewitnesses shows exactly that. ✗ overpowering — used of smells, heat or emotions that are physically too strong; ✗ overriding — 'more important than everything else' (an overriding priority), not strength of proof; ✗ overbearing — describes a bossy, domineering person, not evidence.

items.q: The accountant admitted ______ the invoices but denied knowing that they had been forged.
items.vi: Kế toán viên thừa nhận đã ký các hóa đơn nhưng phủ nhận việc biết chúng là giả.
items.explanation: Admit takes a gerund, and the clue but denied knowing that they had been forged puts the signing before the admission, so the perfect gerund having signed fits. ✗ to sign — admit is never followed by a to-infinitive; ✗ to have signed — a perfect infinitive is still an infinitive, so it fails after admit; ✗ sign — a bare verb cannot be the object of admit.

items.q: The new sentencing guidelines give judges very little ______ to shorten a term for a first-time offender.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn tuyên án mới cho các thẩm phán rất ít khoảng linh hoạt để rút ngắn mức án đối với người phạm tội lần đầu.
items.explanation: The clue very little ______ to shorten a term means very little freedom to act within the rules, which is leeway. ✗ allowance — money paid regularly, or a permitted amount (a baggage allowance); ✗ clearance — official permission (security clearance) or physical space (bridge clearance); ✗ tolerance — willingness to accept behaviour or opinions you dislike, not room to vary a sentence.

items.q: Give me a couple of days to ______ your offer before I hand in my notice at the bank.
items.vi: Hãy cho tôi vài ngày để cân nhắc kỹ lời đề nghị của anh trước khi tôi nộp đơn xin nghỉ việc ở ngân hàng.
items.explanation: The clue give me a couple of days to ______ your offer before I hand in my notice means 'think about it carefully' = mull over. ✗ glaze over — (of eyes) show boredom or tiredness; it takes no object; ✗ hand over — give something to someone else, which makes no sense with an offer you received; ✗ take over — take control of a company or job, not consider an offer.

items.q: The tannery was fined twice last year; ______, it continues to discharge untreated waste into the river.
items.vi: Xưởng thuộc da đã bị phạt hai lần vào năm ngoái; tuy vậy, nó vẫn tiếp tục xả chất thải chưa qua xử lý ra sông.
items.explanation: The tannery was fined twice yet continues to discharge waste, so the second clause contradicts what the fines should have achieved: the concessive adverb nevertheless, which can stand between a semicolon and a comma. ✗ whereas — a conjunction that joins two clauses directly, so it cannot sit between ';' and ','; ✗ therefore — 'as a result', but continued pollution is not a result of the fines; ✗ otherwise — 'if not', which would need the first clause to be a condition.

items.q: ______ afford the rising licence fees, the small radio station switched to streaming its programmes online.
items.vi: Vì không thể trả nổi phí bản quyền ngày càng tăng, đài phát thanh nhỏ đã chuyển sang phát trực tuyến các chương trình của mình.
items.explanation: A present-participle clause gives the reason for the main clause: Being unable to afford = because it was unable to afford. ✗ Been unable to — a past participle cannot open a participle clause without 'having'; ✗ Be unable to — a bare infinitive cannot start a clause of reason; ✗ Having unable to — 'having' must be followed by a past participle (having been unable), not by the adjective 'unable' alone.

items.q: Companies that delay investing in wind power now may well ______ when the government subsidies are withdrawn next year.
items.vi: Những công ty trì hoãn đầu tư vào điện gió lúc này rất có thể sẽ bỏ lỡ cơ hội khi trợ cấp của chính phủ bị rút vào năm tới.
items.explanation: The clue delay investing now … when the subsidies are withdrawn next year describes losing an opportunity by being too slow = miss the boat. ✗ miss the mark — fail to hit the target or achieve the intended result; ✗ miss the point — fail to understand what really matters; ✗ miss a beat — hesitate for a moment, usually in 'without missing a beat'.

items.q: A number of senior engineers ______ resigned since the merger was announced, leaving the department badly understaffed.
items.vi: Nhiều kỹ sư cấp cao đã từ chức kể từ khi vụ sáp nhập được công bố, khiến bộ phận này thiếu nhân lực trầm trọng.
items.explanation: A number of + plural noun means 'several' and takes a plural verb, and since the merger was announced calls for the present perfect: have resigned. ✗ has — singular; that goes with 'the number of' (the number of engineers has fallen); ✗ is — makes a passive 'is resigned', which does not exist; ✗ was — singular and a past passive, wrong on both counts.

items.q: Global coal consumption reached its ______ in 2013 and has been drifting downwards ever since.
items.vi: Mức tiêu thụ than toàn cầu đạt đỉnh vào năm 2013 và đã giảm dần kể từ đó.
items.explanation: A quantity reaches its peak (highest level), and drifting downwards ever since confirms we mean the highest point of a figure. ✗ summit — the top of a mountain, or a meeting of leaders; ✗ climax — the most exciting or decisive moment of a story or event; ✗ crest — the top of a wave or a hill, not a level of consumption.

items.q: The suspect is believed ______ the country on a false passport within hours of the robbery.
items.vi: Nghi phạm được cho là đã rời khỏi đất nước bằng hộ chiếu giả chỉ vài giờ sau vụ cướp.
items.explanation: After is believed / thought / said + infinitive, an action earlier than the belief takes the perfect infinitive, and within hours of the robbery is past, so to have left. ✗ to leave — a simple infinitive refers to the present or future; ✗ having left — a gerund, but this passive reporting pattern requires a to-infinitive; ✗ to be left — a passive, so the suspect would be 'left' by someone.

items.q: Recycling aluminium uses ______ energy than smelting it from raw ore, which is why scrap cans are so valuable.
items.vi: Tái chế nhôm tiêu tốn ít năng lượng hơn nhiều so với luyện từ quặng thô, đó là lý do lon nhôm phế liệu có giá trị đến vậy.
items.explanation: Energy is uncountable, so the comparative before than is less, strengthened by far. ✗ much fewer — fewer is for countable plurals (fewer cans); ✗ very less — very cannot modify a comparative; use much / far / a lot; ✗ the least — a superlative cannot be followed by than.

items.q: When my manager announced that the whole department would be relocating to Iceland, I assumed she was ______.
items.vi: Khi quản lý của tôi thông báo rằng cả phòng sẽ chuyển tới Iceland, tôi cứ tưởng chị ấy đang trêu tôi.
items.explanation: The clue I assumed she was after an unbelievable announcement (relocating to Iceland) means I thought she was joking = pulling my leg. ✗ pulling strings — using secret influence to get something done; ✗ pulling her weight — doing her fair share of the work; ✗ pulling her punches — being gentler or less critical than she could be.

items.q: An independent laboratory has ______ doubt on the company's claim that the leak was contained within hours.
items.vi: Một phòng thí nghiệm độc lập đã đặt nghi vấn về tuyên bố của công ty rằng vụ rò rỉ đã được khống chế trong vài giờ.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is cast doubt on something = make people question it, and the lab is challenging the company's claim. ✗ shed — you shed light on a matter (make it clearer), the opposite idea; ✗ laid — you lay blame on someone, not doubt; ✗ drawn — you draw attention to something, not doubt.

items.q: After weeks of haggling, the delegates finally ______ down the wording of the treaty, ______ that the wealthiest nations would fund the adaptation programme.
items.vi: Sau nhiều tuần mặc cả, các đại biểu cuối cùng cũng chốt được câu chữ của hiệp ước, với điều kiện các quốc gia giàu nhất sẽ tài trợ cho chương trình thích ứng.
items.explanation: Nail down = settle something definitely, and the condition that follows is introduced by provided (that) – the only one of the four conjunctions that can be followed by that. ✗ pinned / unless — 'pin down the wording' is fine, but 'unless that' does not exist; ✗ boiled / in case — 'in case that' is not English, and boil down means reduce to essentials; ✗ narrowed / as long as — 'as long as that' does not exist, and you narrow down a list of choices, not wording.

items.q: Even a minute ______ of the pesticide is enough to kill the bees that pollinate the orchard.
items.vi: Chỉ một liều thuốc trừ sâu rất nhỏ cũng đủ để giết chết những con ong thụ phấn cho vườn cây.
items.explanation: A dose is a measured quantity of a drug or chemical, and of the pesticide … enough to kill confirms that sense. ✗ portion — a part of something, especially an amount of food served; ✗ serving — a helping of food or drink for one person; ✗ ration — a fixed allowance of food or fuel in times of shortage.
